How do products like sticky tape and masking tape work on a molecular level?
Glue based systems adhere to surfaces mechanically by filling voids within the substrate, creating an interlocking behavior between the two. It basically acts like a shitty version of velcro.

Sci Show has a good simple video on the subject, it is due to electorstatic forces, the adhesive itself basically just tries to cover as much surface area as possible to make these forces have a significant effect.

https://youtu.be/fHclnxdmV_g

as an addendum, some adhesive products are actually used to weld the two surfaces together by slightly melting them chemically before hardening. EX. PVC Glue
